fields.description: Issue dominated by coverage and commentary on the September 1928 hurricane and catastrophic flooding in the Lake Okeechobee area, including estimates of loss of life, criticism of state response, and discussion of communications and storm forecasting (including praise of radio/telegraph operators and the Miami weather bureau). Reports and editorials address relief efforts (Red Cross, civic organizations such as the Elks, and local volunteer activity), storm impacts in South Florida communities, and restoration of utilities by Florida Power & Light. Additional local civic and political items include Miami Beach’s upcoming municipal election, Hialeah taxpayer activism and public works, high food prices in Miami, jail procurement concerns, and assorted local crime, prohibition-era liquor market notes, and entertainment/social columns.
